claim: Let \(T\) be any rooted directed tree with \(n\ge3\) vertices and all original arcs pointing away from its unique root. For any vertex \(v\), write \(d(v)\) for its root depth and \(p(v)\) for its parent. Adjoin exactly one new binary prey-to-consumer arc \(u\to v\), with \(v\) not the root, \(u\ne v\), and \(u\ne p(v)\). Define the trophic level of the root to be \(1\), each nonbasal trophic level to be one plus the arithmetic mean of its incoming predecessor levels, and the squared classical trophic-incoherence parameter to be \(q^{2}=n^{-1}\sum_{x\to y}(s_y-s_x-1)^2\), where the sum is over the \(n\) arcs of the augmented graph. Then the new level equations have a unique solution and the exact incoherence depends only on the endpoint depths and whether the new arc closes a directed cycle. If \(v\) is not a proper ancestor of \(u\), the new graph is acyclic and \[q^{2}=\frac{(d(v)-d(u)-1)^{2}}{2n}.\] If \(v\) is a proper ancestor of \(u\), the new graph has one directed cycle, and for \(\ell=d(u)-d(v)\ge1\), \[q^{2}=\frac{2(\ell+1)^{2}}{n}.\] Consequently, among allowed cyclic additions \(q^{2}\ge8/n\), with equality precisely for an added reverse parent-child arc where the target parent is nonbasal. Among acyclic additions, every positive squared incoherence is at least \(1/(2n)\), and the bound is attainable for every \(n\ge3\) by a two-level shortcut on a path. Writing \(a_h\) for the number of tree vertices at depth \(h\), the number of allowed new arcs preserving perfect trophic coherence is exactly \[\sum_{h\ge1}a_h(a_{h-1}-1).\] These are precisely the new links from a vertex at depth \(h-1\) to a nonchild vertex at depth \(h\). The formulas are for unweighted, equally weighted prey links and do not assert dynamical stability or generalize to arbitrary interacting food webs without additional work.
integrity: An exact all-orders algebraic derivation identifies the two exceptional trophic differences and proves the two exhaustive cases. A standalone independent Gaussian-elimination verifier checks 40,322 allowed added arcs on 1,740 rooted-tree instances with rational arithmetic; finite experiments do not replace the proof.
scientific_limitations: Exact only for a binary unweighted rooted out-tree augmented by one new nonroot-target arc, with the classical mean-prey trophic-level definition. It does not establish any dynamical stability claim, and does not address weighted, multiply modified, or general ecological food webs.
title: An exact one-link trophic-incoherence law for rooted food webs
